notes: ASV marginal alternative (*Now when thy words come to pass, what etc.*) read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text is what is aligned.
The phrase `מִשְׁפַּט הַנַּעַר` writes a *the* before each English noun, so rule 29's arthrous count governs rather than its fronting case.

The italic *how* is left `added`, but a materially different reading is available and should be recorded: מַה scopes over both coordinated members of `מַה־יִּהְיֶה מִשְׁפַּט־הַנַּעַר וּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ`, and rule 25 would make *how* the second, discontinuous realization of that one interrogative where the ASV splits the Hebrew clause in two. It is left `added` because the ASV builds a wholly new English clause there and italicizes the word, but the competing reading is defensible.
